indicators.context: Reflection marker the Deadend CLI supervisor prompt tells the model to send before choosing an XSS payload (_vulnerability_playbooks.jinja2:450, included by supervisor.instructions.jinja2:115); the project's own benchmark logs show GET /page?test=deadend7x7probe
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Deadend CLI source code

indicators.context: Password of the shipped test account; pw_send_payload swaps the dummy value deadendpassword for it before sending, so targets receive it in login and sign-up requests (auth_handler.py:23-62). Raw or URL-encoded (%21)
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Deadend CLI source code

indicators.context: User name of the shipped test account sent to targets after the dummy-to-real swap (auth_handler.py:51-55); seen in the project's benchmark logs and reports
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Deadend CLI source code

indicators.context: E-mail of the shipped test account sent to targets after the swap from deadenduser@straylabs.ai (auth_handler.py:45-49). Only account 0 of the wallet is used by default
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Deadend CLI source code

indicators.context: Dummy user name the model is given in v0.1.15 and earlier (request_agent.py:63-80 at that tag). pw_send_payload replaces it, but requests the model sends with curl in the Kali sandbox or with the Python tool keep it, together with the password deadendpassword
indicators.source: ThreatDefence review of the Deadend CLI source code

indicators.context: Credential placeholder the prompts at 34e83717 give the model (also <dummy_username>, <dummy_email>); the swap does not replace these, so a build of this commit sends them to the target as written (inferred from the code, not seen in a capture). May arrive URL-encoded as %3Cdummy_password%3E
